about: A candidate with rules for other players' turns (docs/agents/add_react.py). Only the playbook object is read.

rules.ability: Destroy all artifacts, creatures, and enchantments
Destroy all creatures with power 4 or greater
Remove a loyalty counter from each
At the beginning of your upkeep, this emblem deals 1 damage

playbook.notes:
Version 2 (candidate, not shipped): version 1's rules unchanged and in their order, with answer rules added, written from the 200 games of this seat in league-run #3 (seed 20261250, every seat a bot), where the deck won 29 and Forge's attack sent 15.4 attackers a game at its planeswalkers (walkers left the battlefield for the graveyard 1,029 times in the 171 games it did not win). League figures below are games drawn / cast from hand / in hand at the seat's last turn in a game it did not win. The deck's planeswalkers are all legendary and none is a creature on our side of a wipe, so every wipe in it is close to one-sided for this seat: what it costs us is tokens, mana rocks and the odd creature. At the top, before the turn's other plays, so the board is cleared before new tokens and walkers go down: (1) Urza's Ruinous Blast when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more power than ours, or (2) can attack us for 12 or more and has more power (47/6/31: Forge's AI almost never casts it; it exiles every nonlegendary nonland permanent and leaves our walkers, Guff, Mangara, Kazuul and the Oaths); (3) Blasphemous Act on the same board as (1) (61/38/10; Forge casts it, the rule makes it sure and early); (4) Nevinyrral's Disk's activation on that board (53 drawn, 19 cast, 11 activations; it spares planeswalkers); (5) Chandra, Awakened Inferno's -3 (3 damage to each non-Elemental creature) when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more creatures than we do: never used in the league, Forge took her +2 all 145 times; (6) Elspeth's -3 (destroy each creature with power 4 or more) when one opponent can attack us for 12 or more with 3 creatures or fewer, which means at least one of them has power 4 or more, and has more power than ours: never used in the league (113 +1, 10 -7); (7) Promise of Loyalty when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more power and we have 2 creatures or fewer (74/24/39; version 1's hold until opp_power > power stays, this makes it cast). After the mana rocks, the deterrents to attacks on the walkers: Onakke Oathkeeper at once (57/39/15: a tax of 1 for each creature attacking a walker), Norn's Annex when an opponent has 3 or more creatures (55/29/22), Silent Arbiter on the board of (1) (47/14/17; version 1's hold stays and this rule casts it), Nevinyrral's Disk when an opponent has 3 or more creatures, so it is on the battlefield and untapped by the time (4) wants it. The last list of creatures gains Wall of Denial (49/21/26), Fog Bank (57/43/11), Norn's Annex and the Disk, so they are cast with mana left over whatever the board. Thresholds: 4 creatures is Hail, Caesar's for its one-sided wipe; 12 as a threat is the same as its Ruinous Ultimatum rule; neither was tuned on these games. Left to Forge as before: Path to Exile (57/55/1) and Swords to Plowshares (64/60/3), which it already casts; the single-target loyalty removal (Chandra, Torch -3 64 times, The Wanderer -2 65, Nahiri -2 70, Vronos -2 80). Not expressible: Guff Rewrites History (46 drawn, never cast, 33 in hand at a loss: it needs a target of every player's, which Forge's logic never agrees to) and Semester's End (an instant that saves walkers from attack or removal, wanted on another player's turn).
 Tried and dropped: Gideon Jura's +2 (an opponent's creatures must attack Gideon) when one opponent could attack for 8: it never fired in 8 local tables with Gideon out on 8 turns; the ability targets an opponent, so a rule needs Forge's logic to agree, and Forge's logic for that delayed trigger does not (the card is AI:RemoveDeck:All, its script notes the missing AI). Checked at 16 local tables of bots (seeds 20263040 and 20263041, opponents from bots-v2 under their playbooks; games read in the event log, not playbook_stats): every new rule but the Disk's play rule fired as meant at least once; the wipes took 1 to 9 of our permanents against 4 to 44 of the opponents' (Ruinous Blast 44 against 7 and 26 against 5; Chandra's -3 nine opponent creatures against two of ours). Win rate not measured: 3 wins of 16 is too few games to mean anything. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #32: on the same 200 tables of bots (seed 20261300, opponents drawn from the other eleven bots under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) it won 52 against version 1's 42 (+5.0 points, 95% -1 to +11, exact test 0.13); the cards the new rules name were cast in 446 of the 544 games they were drawn, under version 1 in 247 of 490. It has not been set against its stock pilot. What it still casts in a share of games 15 points or more below stock AI's (the stock arm of ab-run #26, other tables of the same pool), 12 cards: Spark Double, Deepglow Skate, Narset, Enlightened Master, Wall of Denial, Mangara, the Diplomat, Kazuul, Tyrant of the Cliffs and 6 more (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/pool-answers/planeswalker-party-check.txt). VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `hooksopen` (2026-11-21). Version 2 with five changes: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); and then a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); and then when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 3: the `hooksopen` arm of ab-run #62 (seed 20261450, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v30/, DESIGN.md section 40). Beside version 2 on the same 200 tables of the pool: 52 wins against 56 (11 tables against 15, exact test 0.56); the `hooks` arm 61. Read over the five decks together by the rule fixed before the run: the four hooks hold and free damage holds; no deck is left out. VERSION 4 CANDIDATE `guard`. Version 3 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 4: the `guard` arm of ab-run #65 (seed 20261470, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v33/, DESIGN.md section 40). Beside version 3 on the same 200 tables of the pool: 54 wins against 53 (4 tables against 3, exact test 1.00); dead with its own creatures tapped 7 times where it was 8. By the rule fixed before the run the guard goes into the five decks together: it had held for the other seven (ab-run #63) and over the five its tables are not behind (34 against 29). CANDIDATE react (harness 0.4.12, docs/agents/add_react.py): version 4 with Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares kept from Forge's AI and played by rules on other players' turns: at a creature attacking the seat when the attack ends its game through its best blocks and one removal changes that, or when one removal takes 6 damage or more away; otherwise in the end step before the seat's own turn at the most dangerous opponent's best permanent worth 3 or more that the spell can hit. From 3 lands the mana for one of them is kept through the seat's own turn while it has such a target.
